claims.statement: The GraphClient abstraction owns app-only authentication to Microsoft Graph using either managed identity (DefaultAzureCredential) in production or client-secret credentials (tenant_id, client_id, client_secret) in local development, with the credential injected at construction so unit tests can fake it.

Delta pagination via iter_delta_pages() yields one page at a time with its @odata.nextLink, allowing the walker to persist resume_token at page boundaries when budget expires, and returns the terminal @odata.deltaLink as the generator's return value for storage as delta_token once a walk completes.

Content hash retrieval respects a preference order (quickXorHash > sha256Hash > crc32Hash) per ADR-0017, allowing the walker to capture change signals from different drive types (SharePoint/OneDrive-for-Business vs personal OneDrive) without reimplementation.
All Graph failures (auth, HTTP, JSON parsing) are translated to a chained GraphError at the boundary so callers depend on one domain type instead of raw httpx or Azure SDK exceptions.

The MessageQueue abstraction sends and receives Pydantic JSON-serialized Message work items, translating transport and validation failures to chained QueueError, with ReceivedMessage wrapping the parsed Message plus message_id, pop_receipt, and dequeue_count for deletion and poison-message detection.

The Message wire format carries source (sharepoint or filesystem), identity fields (drive_id, drive_item_id), metadata (file_name, mime_type), content_hash for re-validation, and timezone-aware enqueued_at; drive_item_id serves as a source-neutral locator (Graph item id or relative filesystem path).

MessageQueue.receive() marks visibility timeout to hide a message while the processor works; on success the processor calls delete() with message_id and pop_receipt; on failure the message reappears after visibility timeout and its dequeue_count (Azure's redelivery counter) drives retry/poison shedding, never the message field.

The database UPSERT on (sync_state_id, drive_item_id) includes a WHERE classification_override IS NULL guard so the classifier never overwrites a manual override; new files insert, hash changes update with rotation to previous_hash, and overridden files remain untouched.

SyncState manages walker position per library: delta_token (@odata.deltaLink) is stored only on completion as the sync watermark, resume_token (@odata.nextLink) is stored on interruption to resume at page boundary, and the next walk's start priority is resume_token > delta_token > full enumeration.

Document status lifecycle (queued → processing → completed/skipped/failed) tracks per-file processing state; the processor marks processing before attempting classification and writes the terminal outcome (completed, skipped, or failed with error_message and retry_count).

The ContentSource protocol abstracts retrieval: GraphContentSource forwards to GraphClient for fetch_content_hash and download, while FilesystemContentSource resolves root-relative locators and reads from disk, rejecting absolute paths and escape attempts with SourceError.

FilesystemWalker and FilesystemContentSource share hash_bytes(sha256) for change detection: the walker computes hash at enqueue time and stores it in content_hash; the processor re-checks with the same function and skips (lets walker re-enqueue) on mismatch.

Delta pagination is scoped at the Graph level via root_path: None or '/' queries /root/delta (whole drive), while a path like '/Matters' queries /root:/{percent-encoded path}:/delta with each segment percent-encoded and / separators preserved, allowing subtree enumeration without post-walk filtering.

Provider selection is configuration-driven (CLASSIFIER_PROVIDER=anthropic or foundry) and enforced at client-build time in _build_client(), not at Settings load time, so walker jobs that don't classify don't require inference credentials.

Anthropic authentication uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (required); Foundry authentication uses ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE (required) plus either managed identity (DefaultAzureCredential with get_bearer_token_provider) or ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY, with both modes validated as mutually exclusive and complete at load time.

The Classifier uses prompt caching with ephemeral cache_control on the static category block so the category definitions and examples are cached across all calls in a run, achieving a 90% token cost reduction while remaining valid as long as the block is byte-identical.

The Enqueuer's commit-before-enqueue ordering persists the queued document row before calling queue.enqueue(), so a rare send failure leaves an at-most-once gap (stuck queued row, recoverable via pending reset) instead of a duplicate message.

FilesystemWalker performs full re-enumeration without delta/resume tokens (filesystem has no change feed), relying entirely on hash-based idempotency in the shared Enqueuer: unchanged file hashes skip enqueueing, so re-walking unchanged trees produces no messages.

The Enqueuer's enqueue decision (new file, in-flight skip, pending re-classify, or hash change) is identical for both Graph and filesystem producers via shared _should_enqueue() logic, making idempotency byte-for-byte identical across source variants.

Source selection (CLASSIFIER_SOURCE=sharepoint or filesystem) configures both walker and processor: walker selects which producer to run (Graph delta or filesystem re-enumeration), processor selects which ContentSource (GraphContentSource or FilesystemContentSource) to use for retrieval.

GraphSettings and QueueSettings validation requires either managed identity or the full credential set (tenant_id + client_id + client_secret for Graph, connection_string or account_url + managed identity for Queue); a partially configured section fails loudly at load, not silently.

All external-service failures (Graph, Queue, Database, Inference) are translated to domain error types (GraphError, QueueError, PersistenceError, ClassificationError, SourceError) at their boundaries, always chained from the original exception, so the root cause survives in logs and tracebacks.
